answer: A proof-of-stake bond per agent identity stops Sybil farms from paying off. To register, each agent locks collateral that slashes on proven misbehavior, so every extra identity costs real capital. An operator wanting ten thousand fake agents must lock ten thousand bonds at once; when work pays less than the bond yields elsewhere, the ripple of clones only drains the attacker's treasury. Registries tie each identity to one payout channel enciphered under a shared commitment, so a hidden test cipher cannot be answered twice without linking the copies, and yarrow-lean margins get slashed in bulk.
